title: styles.json schema
description: Schema for plugin/data/styles.json — the second axis catalog (the first being masters.json, the third idioms.json). A 'style' is a TRADITION (bebop, bossa nova, gypsy jazz, ...) characterized by signature voicings, rhythmic conventions, and harmonic vocabulary. Per cross-agent agreement (plugin#417 + ellington-systems/ellington-web), structural fields ship first; prescriptive content (the actual lessons) backfills via the quality-axis distillation pipeline change (#419).

schemaVersion.description: Schema version string. Consumers (Ellington StylePreset loader, plugin engine, future tools) MUST gate on this. Breaking changes bump the major (v2, v3, ...). Minor-additive changes that stay backward-compatible do not bump.

summary.description: 1-3 sentences naming the tradition. What you'd tell someone who'd never heard of it.

voicing_style_tag_affinity.description: dict[voicingStyleTag → weight] declaring which tags this style favors. Tags should reference master.principles[].voicingStyleTags or voicing.voicingStyle values that exist in the corpus. Weights are relative (consumer normalizes). Example: {'pass': 0.9, 'bebop': 1.0, 'chromatic-cool': 0.4}.

rhythmic_signature.description: Structured rhythmic characteristics of the style. Free-form by design — Ellington's comparator reads specific keys; new keys can be added without bumping schemaVersion as long as they're additive.

harmonic_signature.description: Structured harmonic characteristics. Same additive-extension pattern as rhythmic_signature.

prescriptive_lessons.description: Per-chord-quality prescriptive lessons for THIS style. Same shape as masters.usage_notes from #415, but indexed by style instead of master. 'In bossa, m7 is voiced with the 9 on top, anticipated on the upbeat of 4, because [rationale].'

divergence_notes.description: Structured cross-style commentary. Consumed by the Ellington cross-style coach to render 'a bebop player would say...' criticism when audio exhibits one style against another's backing.

exemplar_work_ids.description: Optional: which of the master's works[].id best exemplify this style.

exemplar_principle_ids.description: Optional: which of the master's principles[].id best exemplify this style.

example_masters.description: Which corpus masters exemplify this style. The comparator uses these as canonical references.

why_canonical.description: 1-2 sentences: what about this voicing makes it canonically THIS style.

diagnostic_examples.description: 5-10 reference voicings that ARE canonically this style. Training signal for the comparator.

narrative.description: 1-3 sentences explaining how THIS style uses this chord quality. Should be prescriptive enough to guide a player.

voicing_examples.description: voicings[].id references that exemplify the lesson.

source.description: Free text: where this lesson is grounded (book + page, principle id, or 'placeholder').

provenance.description: Same enum as masters.usage_notes.provenance — see schema/masters.schema.json $defs/usage_note.

divergence_note.description: Structured cross-style commentary. Each entry compares THIS style against vs_style: what's shared, what diverges, and a characteristic quote the coach renders verbatim. Per ellington-systems request.

characteristic_quote.description: Rendered verbatim by the LLM coach. Format: short quote in the voice of a player from THIS style critiquing usage in vs_style. Example for bossa vs bebop: 'You're using bebop chords in bossa rhythm — try lifting the density and anticipating the upbeat.'
